typed.rule: Lower-case. Try schedule, phone, bots in that order; the first list with a whole-word phrase in the message wins. The typed text is kept as typed (same limits and secret check as What you do: 12 words, 80 letters) and shown as typed. No match: goal is unsure, but the typed text is still kept and shown, and still goes to the AI line What they want.
typed.tie: A message that hits two lists ("send reminders to my phone every morning") takes the first in order: schedule. Reason: a scheduled job runs without a chat app (results can go to local files, cron.md 19); the chat app comes up later in the docs' order.

questions.left_out: The docs' other use cases (a coding assistant in the terminal, building tools, training models, Python library: learning-path.md 37, 93, 111, 125) are for developers; a typed answer about them gets goal unsure and the docs' order.
questions.changes_later: Rule R3: the goal's thing comes next, before the docs' order (learning-path.md 22: "Have a specific goal? Skip to By Use Case"). It also picks the part of the SEEN line about the goal, and fills the reason in the recommendation.
questions.why_it_earns_place: His own question. It is the one answer that moves a thing ahead of the docs' order. Three answers are the three docs use cases a non-developer can do from the app; with Not sure yet that is four.

look.model_rule: added live-v2-c13. The model part by what setup.runtime_check found, read fresh each time SEEN is built: (1) the check answered: model_ok. (2) a model is set (provider and model named) but the check failed or timed out: model_slow. (3) no provider or model set (for example 'No LLM provider configured'): model_not. (4) the read itself failed: model_unread. model_ok is never the default: when the Builder cannot tell (2) from (3), show model_unread.

inputs.model: ok | not | unread (setup.runtime_check; unread = the read failed or timed out)
inputs.new: new | some | well | skip (Q_NEW; skip also when never answered)
inputs.goal: schedule | phone | bots | unsure (Q_GOAL; unsure also for Not sure yet, skip, a typed answer with no match)
inputs.done: items done = seen done by a read (personality, scheduled_job, second_bot; model is its own input) + said done by the person (kept) + Something else pressed this visit (not kept)

ai.where: Only REC (and BACK_DONE/DONE_SEEN followed by REC) has an AI step. Every question, the look, the choice, the steps and every other line are written lines.
ai.call: One llm call per REC, max_tokens 120, the same 12 s and slow_ai rule as the live answers (helper-talk-live-v2 slow_ai).
handed: work (already sent today as About them)
goal: the picked label or the typed text
the SEEN sentences (facts read, no numbers beyond the job/bot count)
the chosen item's card name and why sentence
not_handed: the steps (they are shown as written lines; the AI never writes them)
ai.change_to_never_sent: Today input.never_sent lists every kept thing but work. This adds goal and new for the REC call only. Reason: they are picked labels or a short typed text, and they are what the reason is made of.
ai.it_may_write: One or two sentences that name {card} and say why it fits this person. Nothing else. Want the steps? and the answers are added in code.

checks.order: no_reply (checks_c5) first, then c26 (notes shown), the existing name check, then s1 to s8. Any fail: the written REC text; a no-reply or 12 s timeout also follows slow_ai.
checks.s1_names_thing: The reply holds the chosen item's name or one of its aliases (any case).
checks.s2_no_other_thing: The reply holds no alias of any other item and no name from the list's later items.
checks.s3_no_steps: None of these words: click, press, tap, open, type, paste, scan, settings, menu, button, tab, ctrl, cmd, terminal, command; no ` and no http or www.
checks.s4_size: At most 35 words and at most 2 sentences.
checks.s7_not_doing_it: No I'll / I will / I can / I could / let me followed within 3 words by set, install, connect, create, make, add, build, do; no set (it) (up) for you, do it for you and the like. A bare for you passes: the list's own why sentence for Scheduled jobs has it.

ai.failed_line: The written REC text, the same as in a build with no AI. Nothing tells the person the AI failed (as the live answers do today), except the slow_ai line once per visit.

typed_answer.rule: At Q_NEW and Q_GOAL, a typed message is kept as the answer only when it reads as an answer. In this order: 1. restart words (restart_phrases, whole words, anywhere in the message): RESTART. 2. Not an answer, never kept: a question (has ?, or starts with one of question_starts), a request to Helper (starts with one of request_starts, or holds one of request_words), or small talk (helper-talk-v2.json small_talk kinds). It is answered by the normal routing, then SETUP_REASK or SETUP_REASK_GOAL asks again (once). 3. Anything else is an answer: kept as typed (Q_GOAL: matched to schedule, phone or bots by the typed lists, else unsure; Q_NEW: well, some, new by its lists, else not kept).
typed_answer.small_talk_note: Small talk here means these helper-talk-v2.json small_talk kinds. Not ok: yes, ok and sure are answers at a question.
typed_answer.answer_note: An answer may still start with "I" or "I want": "I want a morning summary" is kept (schedule). "Can it remind me every morning" starts with can: not kept, it is answered as a question, then Q_GOAL is asked again.

rec_rule_loom: REC is the written sentence only, with no AI ({reason} from reasons, {card} and {why} from the list). It reads the same every time for the same person, and says Hermes, never your assistant. Its {card} is the Dashboard's You are here stop (dash-setup-list-v2.json here_rule).

back_rule.rule: While Q_NEW, Q_GOAL, REC (Want the steps?) or a STEP is the open line, a typed message that holds one of back_words (whole words, after the restart check) means Helper's previous question or step, never Hermes's checkpoints. Helper shows: at STEP n with n > 1: STEP_BACK for step n - 1 (its own answers). Else BACK_ONE, then the first of previous[open line] that was shown in this set-up conversation, as its own bubble with its answers. If none was shown: BACK_FIRST, then the open line once more (one_question.reask). The earlier answer stays kept until a new pick replaces it.
back_rule.order_note: Restart words win first ("lets go back to the start" is RESTART), then back words, then the rest of typed_answer.

one_question.rule: While a set-up question is open (Q_NEW, Q_GOAL, REC, or a STEP) and the person types something that is not an answer, restart words or back words: 1. Helper's answer carries NO offer: no "Do you want ...?" line and no picks under it (offers, near offers and name offers are all dropped). Action buttons of the answer (Open Messaging, Show me what to ask) stay: they are not questions. 2. If the answer would be a topic question (kind question, e.g. "Do you already pay for ChatGPT or Claude?"), Helper shows that topic's plain line instead. 3. Then the open question once more, as its own bubble with its buttons (reask[open line]). Every time, not once only. 4. Exception: if the answer is one of own_question_kinds (it cannot be answered without its own question, e.g. "Do you mean me, or your own Hermes?"), that question is shown with its buttons and the set-up question is NOT added; it comes back (reask) as the next bubble after the person answers that question. So after any message, exactly one question is on screen: the last bubble.
